expected_approaches.summary: Sort by start, maintain one working interval, and emit it only when the next start is beyond its end.
expected_approaches.applicability: Closed intervals that must be returned in start order.
assumptions: Touching endpoints overlap under the stated closed-interval semantics.
key_invariants: Emitted intervals are finalized and non-overlapping.
The working interval is the union of all processed intervals that still overlap it.
expected_approaches.space_complexity: O(n) or O(log n) depending on sorting implementation
tradeoffs: Sorting enables a single merge scan.
common_failure_modes: overwriting end instead of taking max

alternative_approaches.summary: Repeatedly merge overlapping pairs until none remain.
key_invariants: Each merge preserves the covered union.
tradeoffs: Avoids sorting initially but repeatedly revisits intervals.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: vector<vector<int>> merge(vector<vector<int>> intervals){ sort(intervals.begin(),intervals.end()); vector<vector<int>> out; for(auto interval:intervals){if(out.empty()||out.back()[1]<interval[0]) out.push_back(interval); else out.back()[1]=max(out.back()[1],interval[1]);} return out;} };

class Solution { public int[][] merge(int[][] intervals){ java.util.Arrays.sort(intervals,(a,b)->Integer.compare(a[0],b[0])); java.util.List<int[]> out=new java.util.ArrayList<>(); for(int[] interval:intervals){if(out.isEmpty()||out.get(out.size()-1)[1]<interval[0])out.add(interval);else out.get(out.size()-1)[1]=Math.max(out.get(out.size()-1)[1],interval[1]);}return out.toArray(new int[out.size()][]);} }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: Explain the distinct roles of emitted intervals and the working interval.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Derive sorting plus one pass complexity.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Preserve the maximum end for nested intervals.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Sort before relying on local overlap comparisons.

counterexamples.purpose: Closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Half-open endpoint semantics alter whether touching intervals merge.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why sorted starts make one scan sufficient.

expected_good_signals: future intervals cannot begin before current after sorting
sample_phrasings: Why does ordering by start let one scan decide every merge?
What should happen to the current end for [1,4] followed by [2,3]?

expected_good_signals: merges when start equals current end
sample_phrasings: Would your comparison change for half-open intervals?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on the working-interval invariant and endpoint semantics.

reference_reasoning: Sort-and-scan is a strong technical prior, but other correct approaches remain valid when their reasoning and costs are clear.
